column3: The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
The Hebrew uses singular “lamp”; BSB uses plural “lamps.”
The Hebrew says Aaron shall tend singular “it”; BSB uses plural “the lamps.”
The Hebrew says “the pure lampstand,” without explicitly naming gold here; BSB adds “gold.”
The Hebrew names two tenth-measures for each loaf without explicitly naming an ephah; BSB explains them as “two-tenths of an ephah.”
The Hebrew says “the pure table,” without explicitly naming gold here; BSB says “the table of pure gold.”
The Hebrew says to put frankincense “on the row”; BSB says “near each row.”
The Hebrew repeats “on the Sabbath day” twice and uses active singular “he shall arrange it”; BSB says “Every Sabbath day” and uses passive “the bread is to be set out.”
The Hebrew uses “holiness of holinesses” and “a perpetual statute”; BSB uses “a most holy part” and “his portion forever.”
The Hebrew repeats “the son of the Israelite woman” as one of those fighting; BSB uses “him.”
The Hebrew joins blaspheming the Name and cursing with “and”; BSB combines them as blaspheming “with a curse.”
The Hebrew says the clarification will be “by the mouth of the LORD”; BSB supplies “the will of the LORD” instead.
The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he shall “bear his sin”; BSB adds “the consequences of” the sin.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the striking verb with “a human life”; BSB says “takes the life of anyone else.”
The Hebrew uses the striking verb with “an animal’s life”; BSB says “kills an animal.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the giving verb for inflicting a blemish and its reciprocal punishment; BSB uses “injured” and “inflicted.”
The Hebrew repeats the striking verb for animal and human victims; BSB says “kills.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names a “stone” as the means of stoning; BSB gives only the stoning verb.
